    //==
    // # Numeric structures components — the IVector component surface
    //
    // The map/zip/fold combinators over a vector's components, the reductions built
    // on them (SumComponents, Magnitude, Dot), the distinguished elements derived
    // from Broadcast, and the per-concrete-type FromComponents/Broadcast primitives
    // that close the loop. Everything here is written once and applies to every
    // IVector implementor.

    //==
    // # IVector â€” component-wise lifting
    //
    // IVector declares FromComponents and Broadcast and inherits Count/At from
    // IIndexable<Number>, so a vector can be both read as and rebuilt from an
    // Array<Number>. That closes the loop: the Array intrinsics (Map, Zip,
    // Reduce, All, Any) lift straight onto vectors, and every derived body below
    // is written once instead of once per concrete type.
    //
    // As elsewhere in these libraries, the helpers return the bare interface type
    // IVector rather than the concrete implementing type.

    // The components of self as an Array<Number>, in index order.
    ComponentArray(self: IVector): Array<Number>
        => self.Count.Range.Map(i => self[i]);
